OPERATION EMPOWER — MASTER EXECUTION DIRECTIVE
ScaleSmiths Partner Academy, Sales Enablement & Knowledge Infrastructure
Organisation: ScaleSmiths Limited
Repository: https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths
B0 Pull Request: https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155
B1 Planning Pull Request: https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/156
B0 Branch: `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`
B1 Planning Branch: `claude/empower-b1-planning`
B1 Planning Commit: `0786e6d`
B1 Implementation Branch: `feature/operation-empower`
Priority: P0
Objective: Finalise the B0 integration, quality-assure all B1 planning and educational material, obtain the necessary approvals, and implement the ScaleSmiths Partner Academy and Sales Enablement System.
1. EXECUTIVE MISSION
Operation Intelligence B0 has completed substantial engineering and is awaiting final merge governance.
Operation Empower B1 now has a dedicated planning package comprising 27 Markdown documents under:
`docs/expansion/empower/`
The package includes:

* Architecture and implementation design.
* Security model.
* Approval requirements.
* Thirteen proposed Academy courses.
* Ninety-four draft lessons.
* Optional knowledge checks.
* Thirteen professional resource drafts.
* Twelve objection-handling responses.
* Six follow-up templates.
* Thirty-three knowledge entries.
* UI and experience specifications.
* Acceptance criteria.
* Content governance requirements.

These are drafts, not commercially approved publications.
This operation has four objectives:

1. Finish the engineering and governance handoff for B0.
2. Perform a comprehensive factual, technical, editorial and legal-risk review of the B1 planning package.
3. Establish a founder-reviewed, versioned publication framework for all training and sales content.
4. Once B0 is legitimately merged, implement B1 as a complete set of functioning vertical slices.

Do not repeat completed work.
Do not create a second partner platform.
Do not reimplement B0 financial infrastructure.
Do not treat model review as human approval.
Do not invent company policies, commitments, pricing or performance claims.
2. REPOSITORY PREFLIGHT
Before modifying anything, inspect:

* Current `master` SHA.
* PR #155 state.
* PR #156 state.
* Branch heads.
* Merge bases.
* Working tree status.
* Existing worktrees.
* Relevant instructions.
* Latest workflow conclusions.
* Branch protection.
* CODEOWNERS.
* Required reviews.
* Deployment workflows.
* Current approved programme configuration.

Read applicable instructions:

* `AGENTS.md`
* `CLAUDE.md`
* `.entire/agent-guide.md`

Read the B0 documentation:

* `docs/expansion/intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md`
* `docs/expansion/intelligence/B0-RELEASE-VERIFICATION.md`
* `docs/expansion/intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md`
* `docs/expansion/intelligence/PROGRAMME-ALIGNMENT.md`

Read every document in:
`docs/expansion/empower/`
Do not assume filenames from summaries.
Enumerate and inspect the actual 27 files.
The planning worktree was previously:
`D:\tmp\ss-empower`
Preserve the three previously reported uncommitted files in the main checkout if they still exist.
Do not reset, clean, overwrite or amend unrelated work.
Record exact preflight evidence.
3. B0 MERGE GOVERNANCE
PR #155 is the prerequisite for B1 implementation.
The last known B0 implementation had all reported engineering checks passing and included:

* Commercial plan integration.
* Commission accounting.
* Discount allowances.
* Bespoke projects.
* Partner withdrawals.
* Achievement Centre.
* Referral management.
* Prospect allocation.
* Market eligibility.
* Sector exclusivity.
* Partner onboarding.
* Meetings.
* Founding Partner recognition.
* Partner webpages.
* Database integrity improvements.
* Real PostgreSQL concurrency CI.
* Profile entitlement suspension.
* Audited domain release.
* Geographic area classification.

Do not reimplement these components.
Verify current readiness
Confirm:

* Current PR head.
* Required checks.
* Human code-owner review.
* Last-push approval.
* Review conversations.
* Protected-area approval.
* Master freshness.
* Deployment consequences.

If the human approval is absent, the merge is blocked.
Do not:

* Self-approve.
* Submit model approval as human approval.
* Dismiss valid required reviews.
* Disable branch protection.
* Modify CODEOWNERS to bypass the requirement.
* Use administrator override.
* Force-push an alternative merge route.
* Merge with unresolved mandatory checks.

Human reviewer handoff
Prepare a focused reviewer package covering:

* Financial invariants.
* Migrations 0073–0090, subject to actual current state.
* PostgreSQL privileges.
* Expansion concurrency.
* Geographic exclusivity.
* Prospect allocation.
* Public profile projection.
* Profile revocation.
* Domain release.
* CI workflow changes.
* Backup and rollback.
* Production deployment triggers.

Request an appropriately authorised independent human review where available.
Clearly identify any governance issue that makes a qualifying review impossible.
If the code owner is also the PR author and GitHub requires another approver, report the exact issue and recommend a legitimate owner-administered governance solution.
Do not implement a workaround autonomously.
B0 merge
The founders authorise merging B0 only after all mandatory reviews, checks and deployment safeguards are satisfied.
If the legitimate conditions become satisfied:

1. Verify the exact head again.
2. Verify the latest relevant CI.
3. Verify code-owner approval after the last push.
4. Verify branch protection.
5. Verify production deployment implications.
6. Merge using the approved repository strategy.
7. Verify the new master commit.
8. Verify post-merge workflows.
9. Verify protected feature flags remain disabled.
10. Record the complete evidence.

If merging master triggers production deployment, do not proceed without separate approval for that consequence.
If the merge cannot proceed, do not begin B1 application engineering.
Continue only the independent B1 documentation audit and preparation work.
4. B1 PLANNING PR MANAGEMENT
PR #156 is currently stacked on the B0 branch.
It must not be merged into the B0 feature branch as a workaround for the missing B0 approval.
While B0 remains unmerged:

* Keep PR #156 open.
* Preserve its documented work.
* Continue safe documentation-only improvements.
* Do not change B1's target to master if doing so would create an inappropriate combined diff.
* Do not merge it prematurely.

Once B0 merges:

1. Fetch the new master.
2. Re-evaluate PR #156's diff and merge base.
3. Retarget PR #156 to master where appropriate.
4. Rebase or update the planning branch only when needed and safe.
5. Verify the 27-document planning package remains intact.
6. Run documentation checks.
7. Run relevant PR checks.
8. Obtain applicable human approval.
9. Merge PR #156 only after its own required gates are satisfied.
10. Verify the resulting master commit.

Do not silently override unresolved content or governance concerns.
If the planning package has factual or technical defects, correct them on the planning branch and preserve an auditable review history.
5. COMPLETE B1 FACTUAL AUDIT
The original planning author explicitly stated that the 27 documents were not independently read back for full factual accuracy.
This is a material outstanding quality requirement.
Perform a complete read-back of every document.
Do not rely on headings, summaries or sampled sections.
Audit every:

* Course.
* Module.
* Lesson.
* Quiz answer.
* Resource.
* Knowledge entry.
* Objection response.
* Follow-up template.
* Technical claim.
* Commercial claim.
* Programme description.
* Approval label.
* Founder decision.
* Security assumption.

Create an evidence-backed content review register.
Each finding must include:

* Source document.
* Heading or content identifier.
* Statement or claim under review.
* Source of authority.
* Finding classification.
* Risk.
* Recommended correction.
* Whether correction was implemented.
* Remaining required approval.

Use these classifications:

* VERIFIED.
* CORRECTED.
* UNSUPPORTED.
* REQUIRES FOUNDER DECISION.
* REQUIRES LEGAL REVIEW.
* REQUIRES ACCOUNTING REVIEW.
* REQUIRES PRIVACY REVIEW.
* DEFERRED.

Do not silently replace genuine company policy with generic best practices.
6. COMMERCIAL CLAIMS AUDIT
Commercial accuracy is a priority.
Verify every relevant reference to:

* Standard website build pricing.
* Monthly Growth Partnership pricing.
* Twelve-month minimum term.
* Historical six-month terms.
* Total contractual commitment.
* £705 standard acquisition commission.
* Growth Partnership-only acquisition.
* Bespoke project commissions.
* Flexible deposits.
* Discount allowances.
* Existing-customer additional work.
* Commission eligibility.
* Refunds.
* Withdrawals.
* Achievement rewards.
* Referral rewards.
* Partner exclusivity.
* Market eligibility.
* Founding Partner recognition.

Use the current authoritative commercial configuration and the B0 accepted-term architecture.
Distinguish:

* Current proposed standard offer.
* Historical accepted agreements.
* Founder-approved exceptions.
* Illustrative earnings.
* Conditional rewards.
* Disabled features.
* Pending policies.

Do not describe proposed achievement or referral payments as immediately payable.
Do not suggest ongoing monthly commission exists where only the initial eligible retainer payment earns acquisition commission.
Do not invent minimum withdrawal amounts or frequency.
Do not guarantee earnings.
Do not claim all countries are commercially activated.
Treat contract, employment-status, VAT and tax matters as requiring proper professional approval.
7. TECHNICAL ACCURACY AUDIT
Review every technical claim.
Prioritise:

* Next.js.
* React.
* Responsive design.
* Website performance.
* SEO.
* AI search optimisation.
* Accessibility.
* Hosting.
* DNS.
* Email.
* Security.
* Backups.
* Analytics.
* WordPress migration.
* Redirects.
* E-commerce.
* CRM systems.
* Booking platforms.
* Business automation.
* Mobile applications.
* Bespoke enterprise software.

Distinguish general technical possibilities from services that ScaleSmiths actually offers under an approved scope.
Do not claim:

* Guaranteed search rankings.
* Guaranteed website traffic.
* Guaranteed enquiries.
* Guaranteed conversion growth.
* Guaranteed zero downtime.
* Guaranteed compatibility with all external systems.
* Universal accessibility certification.
* Unlimited maintenance.
* Unlimited technical support.
* Unlimited hosting resources.
* Automatic security immunity.

Where technical feasibility depends on discovery, make that explicit.
Ensure partners understand when to involve the technical founder.
Any unconfirmed service specification must remain draft.
8. EDITORIAL QUALITY AUDIT
Review the content as a professional learning and sales programme.
Correct:

* Repetition.
* Inconsistent terminology.
* Ambiguous explanations.
* Excessive jargon.
* Poor lesson sequencing.
* Unsupported claims.
* Contradictory examples.
* Incorrect quiz answers.
* Unrealistic client conversations.
* Weak objection handling.
* Missing escalation guidance.
* Inappropriate sales language.

Use British English consistently.
Maintain a confident, professional ScaleSmiths voice.
Avoid manipulation.
Avoid fabricated urgency.
Avoid disparaging competitors.
Avoid promising outcomes that depend on external platforms.
Keep lessons clear enough for inexperienced independent partners while providing useful detail for experienced professionals.
Use real examples only where appropriately sourced and authorised.
Clearly label synthetic examples.
9. COURSE-BY-COURSE VALIDATION
Validate all thirteen planned Academy courses.
For every course:

* Confirm objectives match actual lessons.
* Confirm lessons follow a logical progression.
* Confirm technical explanations are accurate.
* Confirm knowledge checks test the intended concepts.
* Confirm answers are supported by the lesson.
* Confirm resources are relevant.
* Confirm escalation guidance is appropriate.
* Confirm commercial claims match approved or proposed policy.
* Confirm the training remains voluntary.
* Confirm publication approval is pending where applicable.

Preserve the original curriculum structure unless a material issue justifies changing it.
Do not remove useful content merely to shorten the package.
Track all 94 lessons in a content inventory.
Report missing or duplicated lesson identifiers.
10. RESOURCE CENTRE AUDIT
Review all thirteen professional resource drafts.
Verify:

* Audience suitability.
* Commercial accuracy.
* Technical accuracy.
* Privacy requirements.
* Founder approval status.
* Client-facing versus partner-only classification.
* Historical versus current commercial terms.
* Version.
* Review date.
* Related Academy modules.

Check that the material will be useful in real client conversations.
Create a clear publication priority order.
Suggested priority:

1. Company brochure.
2. Website development guide.
3. Growth Partnership guide.
4. Discovery questionnaire.
5. Meeting preparation checklist.
6. Objection handling.
7. Bespoke software overview.
8. Technical escalation guide.
9. Commercial and commission references.
10. Remaining specialist resources.

These priorities may be adjusted based on actual content readiness.
Do not publish the drafts.
11. KNOWLEDGE BASE AUDIT
Audit all thirty-three knowledge entries.
Verify:

* Question.
* Approved or draft answer.
* Client-friendly explanation.
* Technical limitations.
* Source.
* Related resources.
* Escalation instructions.
* Publication status.

Check category coverage and terminology.
Identify gaps in common partner questions.
Recommend additional entries only where they materially improve the initial release.
Do not inflate the library with generic filler.
Use current approved knowledge as the authority.
Where no approved answer exists, display an accurate unresolved state.
12. OBJECTION HANDLING AND COMMUNICATION
Review twelve objection responses and six follow-up templates.
Ensure responses are:

* Truthful.
* Respectful.
* Technically accurate.
* Commercially accurate.
* Useful in realistic conversations.
* Consistent with independent partner status.

Each objection response should distinguish:

* Customer concern.
* Recommended response.
* Supporting explanation.
* Relevant questions.
* Limitations.
* Escalation.
* Applicable approved resource.

Do not use invented case studies or testimonials.
Do not encourage misleading comparisons.
Do not promise discounts without founder approval.
Do not pressure customers into twelve-month agreements through concealed terms.
Keep communications professional and adaptable.
13. FOUNDER APPROVAL REGISTER
Consolidate the existing approval requirements.
Create a clear founder decision register for B1.
Required decisions include:
Commercial

* Service descriptions.
* Standard prices.
* VAT wording.
* Hosting pricing.
* SEO and AEO scope.
* Analytics scope.
* Maintenance boundaries.
* Discount authority.
* Bespoke scoping authority.

Legal and partner governance

* Independent contractor status.
* Voluntary Academy participation.
* Training progress and privacy.
* Partner communications.
* Approved earnings examples.
* Territory claims.
* Referral and achievement descriptions.

Privacy

* Learning progress data.
* Retention.
* Resource download logging.
* Partner access.
* Consent where appropriate.
* Public-facing resources.

Publication

* Approved Academy lessons.
* Approved brochures.
* Approved technical articles.
* Approved objection responses.
* Review intervals.
* Withdrawal and correction procedure.

Do not mark any decision approved without genuine authorised evidence.
Design the system so content can be implemented and tested before the material itself is authorised for publication.
14. ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT
The planning audit identified the admin application's muted text colour:
`#667085`
Its reported contrast against the relevant background is approximately 3.71:1.
Verify the actual rendered background and colour combination.
For normal-size text, WCAG AA generally requires 4.5:1 contrast.
Identify every affected component.
Recommend a suitable accessible palette adjustment consistent with ScaleSmiths branding.
Ensure:

* Keyboard navigation.
* Visible focus.
* Proper headings.
* Accessible form labels.
* Meaningful errors.
* Reduced-motion support.
* Mobile readability.
* Appropriate text contrast.
* Responsive layouts.
* Screen reader semantics.

Do not make an unreviewed global colour change that damages unrelated application components.
During planning, record the proposed change.
During implementation, apply it with visual and accessibility regression tests.
15. CONTENT ARCHITECTURE
Reuse the existing resource infrastructure where appropriate.
The current platform reportedly supports immutable published resource versions but lacks complete approval metadata and review scheduling.
Design and implement the smallest coherent extension.
Content must support:

* Draft.
* Submitted for review.
* Changes requested.
* Approved.
* Published.
* Superseded.
* Archived.
* Withdrawn.

Not every content type needs every state if an existing model supports a simpler secure lifecycle.
Record:

* Author.
* Approver.
* Approval date.
* Publication version.
* Effective date.
* Review due date.
* Audience.
* Source.
* Approval notes.
* Correction history.
* Audit events.

Published versions should remain immutable.
Corrections create new approved versions.
Do not allow ordinary partners to publish official ScaleSmiths guidance.
Do not grant content editors access to financial or commission administration.
16. SEARCH ARCHITECTURE
Use PostgreSQL full-text search for the initial B1 implementation.
Support:

* Search ranking.
* Category filters.
* Approved content only.
* Version-aware results.
* Related resources.
* Founder-managed synonyms.
* Search by service.
* Search by common customer questions.

Do not introduce:

* Paid AI APIs.
* Autonomous agents.
* A vector database.
* External search services.

Unless a measured requirement justifies them.
Implement a secure bounded query model.
Prevent cross-audience content leakage.
Ensure draft content cannot be retrieved through partner search.
Record search-related acceptance criteria.
17. B1 INTERFACE DESIGN
Use the existing admin design system.
Required views:

1. Academy dashboard.
2. Course catalogue.
3. Course and lesson viewer.
4. Resource Centre.
5. Technical Knowledge Base.
6. Objection Handling.
7. Founder Content Studio.

Use official ScaleSmiths branding:

* Black.
* Charcoal.
* Metallic gold.
* Silver.
* Clear typography.
* Restrained animation.

The interface should look like a premium ScaleSmiths application, not a generic third-party learning management system.
Group navigation logically.
Ensure mobile usability at 320px and 390px.
Do not introduce excessive navigation clutter.
Do not display fictional course completion percentages.
18. IMPLEMENTATION GATE
B1 application code may only be developed after:

1. B0 has been legitimately merged into master.
2. The merge commit has been verified.
3. Master CI has been verified.
4. No unauthorised production deployment occurred.
5. PR #156 has been reconciled with the merged foundation.
6. The approved planning baseline is available on the implementation branch.
7. Repository governance requirements are satisfied.

If these conditions are not met, continue the permitted documentation and approval work.
Do not build B1 on the old B0 feature branch.
Do not build B1 on an unapproved substitute branch.
19. B1 IMPLEMENTATION
When the implementation gate is satisfied, create:
`feature/operation-empower`
from the verified master branch.
Develop complete vertical slices.
B1.1 — Content governance

* Versioned publishing.
* Founder review.
* Approval records.
* Review dates.
* Audience restrictions.
* Audit history.

B1.2 — Academy

* Courses.
* Modules.
* Lessons.
* Optional knowledge checks.
* Progress.
* Partner learning interface.

B1.3 — Resource Centre

* Approved resources.
* Categories.
* Search.
* Downloads.
* Founder management.

B1.4 — Knowledge Base

* Approved articles.
* Deterministic full-text search.
* Synonyms.
* Related content.
* Source attribution.

B1.5 — Objection Handling

* Searchable responses.
* Customer-friendly language.
* Discovery questions.
* Escalation guidance.

B1.6 — Integration

* Onboarding toolkit.
* Prospect discovery.
* Meeting preparation.
* Commission documentation.
* Partner dashboard.

B1.7 — Verification

* Unit tests.
* PostgreSQL integration.
* Browser acceptance.
* Accessibility.
* Restricted-role security.
* Financial regression.
* Independent review.
* Draft PR.

Complete one usable feature slice before starting the next.
Do not stop at empty tables or placeholder screens.
20. SECURITY AND PRIVACY
Preserve B0's existing security architecture.
Required protections:

* Founder-controlled publication.
* Partner audience isolation.
* Draft isolation.
* Version integrity.
* Revoked partner denial.
* Resource permission enforcement.
* Bounded file rendering.
* Safe downloads.
* Secure source links.
* Audit history.
* Learning progress privacy.
* Appropriate retention.

Treat Academy progress as personal information.
Training is voluntary and must remain separate from acquisition commission eligibility.
Do not expose individual training completion to other partners.
Avoid arbitrary file uploads unless a secure upload, scanning and serving pipeline exists.
Do not introduce new paid infrastructure unnecessarily.
21. TESTING AND ACCEPTANCE
Run full appropriate verification.
Required:

* Admin unit tests.
* Web unit tests.
* Real PostgreSQL integration.
* Expansion concurrency.
* Restricted database role tests.
* Original Expansion journey.
* B0 partner journey.
* £705 standard commission reconciliation.
* Content publication tests.
* Draft isolation tests.
* Course progress tests.
* Knowledge search tests.
* Resource access tests.
* Objection response tests.
* Founder permission tests.
* Revoked partner tests.
* Accessibility tests.
* Typecheck.
* Lint.
* Production builds.
* Migration checks.
* Repository gates.

Browser acceptance must demonstrate:

1. Founder creates draft course.
2. Founder adds module and lesson.
3. Founder submits content for approval.
4. Authorised founder approves.
5. Course is published.
6. Partner logs in.
7. Partner opens Academy.
8. Partner completes an optional lesson.
9. Progress is persisted.
10. Partner searches knowledge.
11. Partner opens a related resource.
12. Partner searches an objection.
13. Draft-only content remains inaccessible.
14. Founder publishes an updated version.
15. Partner receives the approved version.
16. Revoked partner access is denied.

Use actual production builds and disposable synthetic data.
Distinguish API setup from browser interaction.
22. INDEPENDENT REVIEW
Perform a fresh independent model review where available.
Review:

* Content correctness.
* Commercial claims.
* Publication permissions.
* Versioning.
* Search leakage.
* Resource access.
* Learning progress privacy.
* Database privileges.
* Accessibility.
* Financial regression.

Resolve confirmed critical and high issues.
Document medium and low findings.
Do not claim human review if none occurred.
Do not mark legally sensitive training material approved merely because technical review passed.
23. GITHUB WORKFLOW
For the planning package:

* Push approved documentation-only corrections to the existing planning branch.
* Update PR #156.
* Preserve an accurate diff.
* Keep the required review process.
* Retarget to master after B0 merges.
* Do not auto-merge.

For B1 implementation:

* Work on `feature/operation-empower`.
* Commit completed vertical slices.
* Push using repository-approved workflow.
* Open a draft PR when implementation is reviewable.
* Inspect remote CI.
* Do not merge or deploy B1 automatically.

No changes to branch protection without authorised governance approval.
24. DELIVERABLES
Before B0 merges
Produce:

* Full content accuracy audit.
* Lesson-by-lesson inventory.
* Technical claims review.
* Commercial claims review.
* Editorial corrections.
* Updated resource drafts.
* Knowledge Base review.
* Objection-response review.
* Founder approval register.
* Accessibility review.
* Updated B1 implementation specification.
* PR #156 documentation update.
* Clear B0 merge blocker status.

After B0 merges
Produce:

* Operational Academy.
* Resource Centre.
* Knowledge Base.
* Objection Handling workspace.
* Founder Content Studio.
* Versioned publishing.
* Optional learning progress.
* Restricted-role verification.
* Authenticated browser acceptance.
* Security review.
* B1 draft PR.
* Final implementation report.

Use accurate status labels:

* COMPLETE.
* PARTIAL.
* BLOCKED.
* NOT STARTED.
* DEFERRED.

Do not report B1 implementation complete based solely on documentation.
25. FINAL EXECUTION RULES
Work independently within authorised boundaries.
Do not repeatedly ask for decisions already documented.
Do not fabricate missing founder approvals.
Do not bypass required code-owner review.
Do not merge when required checks or approvals are missing.
Do not enable real partner activation.
Do not activate financial rewards.
Do not execute payouts.
Do not deploy without specific approval.
Do not automatically publish draft educational material.
Do not consume paid AI APIs.
Do not begin B2, B3, B4, B5 or B6.
Prioritise:

1. Factual accuracy.
2. Commercial integrity.
3. Security.
4. Founder control.
5. Partner usability.
6. Implementation quality.
7. Evidence-backed verification.

Complete as much independent work as possible without violating the B0 merge gate.
When an external dependency prevents progress, stop only the dependent work and continue independent authorised tasks.
Do not falsely claim completion.
FINAL DIRECTIVE
Operation Intelligence has built the commercial foundation.
Operation Empower must make it genuinely useful.
First, complete the legitimate B0 merge.
Preserve independent human oversight.
Quality-assure the entire B1 planning package.
Correct unsupported commercial and technical claims.
Establish founder-controlled publication.
Build the Partner Academy.
Build the Resource Centre.
Build the Technical Knowledge Base.
Build the Objection Handling system.
Give ScaleSmiths partners the tools and understanding they need to represent the business professionally.
Do not turn draft content into public commitments.
Do not weaken the financial foundation.
Do not compromise partner independence.
Do not circumvent GitHub protections.
Do not deploy or activate real commercial operations.
OPERATION EMPOWER — MASTER DIRECTIVE
BUILD THE KNOWLEDGE. EQUIP THE PARTNERS. SCALE THE FUTURE.
Commence.

# Operation Empower: B1 planning package

**Package status: DRAFT. Nothing in this folder is approved, published or available to partners or clients.**

Operation Empower prepares two partner capabilities for engineering:

- the **Partner Academy**, an optional, voluntary learning area inside the Partner Portal; and
- the **Sales Resource Centre**, an approved-content library and knowledge base that partners search before speaking to a prospect.

This is B1 research, architecture and content design only. It changes no application code, migrations, authentication, CI or production systems. Implementation must not start until B0 ([PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155), branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`) is merged. Its readiness record is [B0-MERGE-READINESS.md](../intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md).

## Contents

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [PLATFORM-AUDIT.md](PLATFORM-AUDIT.md) | The existing systems Empower reuses, with file references and gaps |
| [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) | Proposed data model, content lifecycle, deterministic search and integration points |
| [SECURITY-MODEL.md](SECURITY-MODEL.md) | Roles, audience separation, publication controls, threats and mitigations |
| [CURRICULUM.md](CURRICULUM.md) | The 13 Academy courses: objectives, modules, lesson outlines, knowledge checks, resources and review requirements |
| [LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md](LESSONS-FOUNDATIONS.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 1 to 6 (company and services) |
| [LESSONS-PRACTICE.md](LESSONS-PRACTICE.md) | Initial lesson content, courses 7 to 13 (selling, policy and conduct) |
| [resources/README.md](resources/README.md) | The 13 Resource Centre drafts, one file each |
| [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md) | Approved-content architecture and the knowledge article inventory |
| [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md) | Visual language, tokens and components, reconciled with the existing design systems |
| [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md) | Wireframe descriptions for the seven key screens |
| [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) | Every item in this package with its approval status, owner and blocking effect |
| [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md) | Proposed delivery phases and their entry and exit gates |
| [ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md](ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA.md) | Testable acceptance criteria for each phase |

## Status vocabulary

Every item in this package carries one of these labels. The register lists them all.

| Label | Meaning | May a partner use it? |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED` | The wording or figure is already published on the public site from a founder-maintained source in the repository (for example `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts` or `web/src/lib/faq-library.ts`). Empower restates it; it does not create it. | Only once an Academy or resource version containing it is approved and published |
| `CONFIRMED: PUBLISHED, OWNER REVIEW` | Published, but the source marks it `ownerReview: true`, so founders should confirm it before it is expanded | No, until confirmed |
| `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` | A fact about how the software behaves, verified in B0 source. It is not commercial approval | Not on its own |
| `PROPOSED POLICY` | A commercial or legal position that exists in B0 drafts or the draft `/partners` page but is not approved (for example the 30% acquisition commission) | No. Must always be labelled as proposed |
| `DRAFT` | Written in this package. Needs founder review | No |
| `FOUNDER DECISION` | Content cannot be finalised until a founder or adviser decides | No |
| `BLOCKED` | Waiting on an external prerequisite, such as the B0 merge or legal advice | No |

No item in this package is `APPROVED`. That status exists only in the future publishing workflow (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)), where a founder records it against an immutable content version.

## Content rules applied throughout

These rules come from the B0 programme sources and the public-site content policy. They apply to every draft here and to every future edit.

1. **No guaranteed outcomes.** No ranking, traffic, enquiry, revenue or earnings guarantees. The source position is published at `faq-library.ts` (`ranking-guarantees`) and on `/partners` ("No guaranteed earnings").
2. **No invented proof.** No testimonials, quotes, statistics or client names beyond the published work listed in `web/src/lib/data.ts`. Partner reuse of published case studies still needs founder permission (see [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md)).
3. **Prices are the published starting prices only**: website from £2,000, Growth Partnership from £350 per month, Business Growth Audit £395, business email from £15 per month. Always paired with the starting-price boundary (`STARTING_PRICE_BOUNDARY`). GBP only.
4. **Commission and rewards are proposed, never promised.** Figures in `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` are illustrations of the proposed programme. Every plan is disabled by default and no reward is payable.
5. **Independence is preserved.** The Academy is optional and voluntary, as the programme states. No course is compulsory and no completion affects commission, allocation or standing. An employment solicitor should confirm this (register item `AP-GOV-02`).
6. **Partner-only and client-facing material are kept apart.** Client-facing material never contains commission, founder-only or internal information.
7. **Escalate rather than improvise.** Where an answer depends on scope, contract or technical review, the content says so and names the escalation route.

## Relationship to existing registers

This package extends, and does not replace, the B0 registers:

- [FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md): commercial, legal and operational decisions;
- [CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](../intelligence/CONTENT-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md): content not yet written (much of which this package now drafts);
- [COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md](../hardening/COMMERCIAL-ACTIVATION-GATES.md): release modes and gates.

When the founders approve an Empower item, record it in [FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md](FOUNDER-APPROVAL-REGISTER.md) and, where it resolves a row there, in the matching B0 register.
# Platform audit: reusable systems for Empower

**Status: DRAFT.** Audited against B0 head `4e713e5` (branch `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95`). Facts below are `CONFIRMED: SYSTEM BEHAVIOUR` unless marked otherwise. Anything not inspected is marked "not verified".

## Summary

The B0 Partner Portal already has the essential primitives for a Resource Centre: a versioned, immutable, audience-tagged resource table with a database-enforced publication lifecycle, a founder publishing form, a partner search box and an onboarding toolkit item reserved for the Academy. What is missing is structure (courses, lessons, knowledge articles with fields), approval evidence (who approved which version, and when it must be reviewed again), progress tracking and a proper search index. Empower should **extend these patterns, not replace them**.

## 1. Partner Portal (admin app, `/partner`)

| Aspect | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Location | Lives on the existing admin origin. No separate subdomain or authentication stack | `web/src/lib/partner-programme.ts` (`partnerLoginUrl`), `admin/src/app/partner/page.tsx` |
| Role | `independent_partner` holds exactly one capability, `expansion.partner` | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:28` |
| Route guard | `/partner` and `/partner/*` map to `expansion.partner`; `/api/partner*` is the only API family that capability reaches | `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:53`, `:99` |
| Workspace | One client component with tabs: Overview, Prospects & scope, Resource library, Commission centre, Achievements, My web page, Referrals, Onboarding, Meetings | `admin/src/components/expansion/ExpansionWorkspace.tsx:67` |
| Styling | Scoped `ex-*` classes in `expansion.css`: panels, badges, `details`-based resource rows, list rows | `admin/src/components/expansion/expansion.css` |
| Server guard | Partner reads run in a transaction behind `requireCapability("expansion.partner")` and `partnerGuard`, which share-locks the user row | `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts:31-52` |

**Reuse:** add Academy and Resource Centre as new workspace areas (or child routes under `/partner`) behind the same capability. **Gap:** the workspace is a single large component; new areas should be separate route segments so they can be code-split and tested independently (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)).

## 2. Founder administration (`/expansion`)

- Route `/expansion` requires `expansion.manage`; founder-only actions use `expansion.founder`. Owner and administrator roles exclude `expansion.partner`, so a founder account never doubles as a partner (`admin/src/lib/rbac.ts:26-27`).
- The founder workspace already includes Recruitment, Programme, Partner operations, Research and allocation, Recognition, Web pages and Delivery capacity tabs.

# Empower architecture (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** This is a design proposal for engineering review after B0 merges. No table, route or migration described here exists. Migration numbers are not reserved.

## 1. Goals and non-goals

**Goals**

1. Partners can find approved answers, resources and training quickly, and can tell at a glance what is approved, for whom, and until when.
2. Founders can draft, review, approve, publish, supersede and retire every content item, with evidence and an audit trail.
3. Partner-only and client-facing material can never be confused or cross-published by accident.
4. The Academy is optional and voluntary, and progress never affects commission, allocation, recognition or standing.

**Non-goals for B1 and the first build**

- No AI generation, AI answers, embeddings or paid AI APIs.
- No assessment that gates anything, no certification, no leaderboard.
- No file uploads, video hosting or third-party learning platform.
- No change to commission, markets, exclusivity or any B0 financial path.
- No client portal delivery of client-facing resources (a later, separate decision).

## 2. Building blocks

```
            Founder administration (/expansion → Content)                Partner Portal (/partner)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Draft editor → Review → Approve → Publish        │      │ Academy   Resources   Knowledge search  │
  │ Supersede / Archive / Review-due queue           │      │ Objection workspace   My progress       │
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘      └───────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
                  │ expansion.founder (writes)                                  │ expansion.partner (reads)
                  ▼                                                             ▼
        content service (server only)  ──────────── published, partner-audience, in-review-window rows only
                  │
                  ▼
  PostgreSQL: content_items · content_versions · content_approvals · content_links
              academy_courses · academy_modules · academy_lessons · academy_progress
              knowledge_entries · search documents (tsvector)
```

All reads and writes go through server functions in the admin app, following the existing `requireCapability` and `partnerGuard` pattern in `admin/src/lib/server/expansion-operations.ts`. There is no client-supplied filter on audience or status.

## 3. Proposed data model

The model generalises `expansion_resources` (immutable versions, database-enforced lifecycle) and adds approval evidence modelled on the public-claims registry (`verifiedAt`, `reviewExpiresAt`, permitted placement).

### 3.1 Content families and versions

| Table | Purpose | Key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `empower_content_items` | A stable identity for one piece of content across versions (for example "Objection: too expensive") | `id`, `kind ∈ {resource, lesson, knowledge, objection, template}`, `slug` (unique), `audience ∈ {partner_only, client_facing}`, `owner_role`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_versions` | Immutable content. Never updated except `status`; never deleted | `id`, `item_id`, `version` (unique per item), `title`, `body` (restricted Markdown), `fields jsonb` (kind-specific, validated), `source_refs jsonb` (list of repository paths or approved documents), `status ∈ {draft, in_review, approved, published, superseded, archived}`, `created_by`, `created_at` |
| `empower_content_approvals` | Append-only approval evidence | `id`, `version_id`, `decision ∈ {approved, changes_requested, rejected}`, `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `reference` (founder decision reference), `review_by date`, `notes` |
| `empower_content_links` | Typed relationships | `from_item`, `to_item`, `relation ∈ {supports_lesson, see_also, escalates_to, replaces}` |

Lifecycle, enforced by a trigger like `expansion_resource_lifecycle`:

```
draft ──► in_review ──► approved ──► published ──► superseded
  │           │                         │
  └──► archived ◄──────── changes ──────┴──► archived
```

- `in_review → approved` requires an `empower_content_approvals` row with `decision='approved'` by a user holding `expansion.founder`, and it must be a **different** founder from the version's author when two founders are active (founder decision `AP-GOV-04`).
- `approved → published` is a separate action, so approval and release can be scheduled apart.
- Publishing version N of an item moves the previously published version to `superseded` in the same transaction. There is at most one published version per item (partial unique index).
- A published version whose `review_by` date has passed is **not served to partners** (fail closed) and appears in the founder "review due" queue. This mirrors `reviewExpiresAt` in `web/src/lib/public-claims.ts`.
- `audience` belongs to the item, not the version, so a new version cannot quietly change who sees it. Changing audience means creating a new item.

### 3.2 Academy

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `empower_courses` | Course identity, order, summary, `content_item_id` for its description |
| `empower_modules` | Ordered modules within a course |
| `empower_lessons` | Ordered lessons; each points at a lesson `content_item` (so lesson text uses the same versioning and approval) |
| `empower_knowledge_checks` | Optional questions per lesson, stored in the lesson version's `fields` |
| `empower_progress` | `partner_id`, `lesson_item_id`, `version_id` read, `opened_at`, `completed_at`, `check_attempted bool` |

Rules:

- **Progress is private to the partner** and visible to founders only in aggregate (counts per course), unless the partner chooses to share it (founder decision `AP-GOV-03`). Progress has no foreign key to, or query from, any commission, allocation, recognition or achievement table, matching the meetings design in [PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md](../intelligence/PARTNER-OPERATIONS.md).
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored, only "attempted". No score is persisted.
- When a lesson is superseded, progress stays attached to the version that was read, and the lesson shows "updated since you read it".

### 3.3 Knowledge entries

A knowledge entry is a `content_item` of kind `knowledge`. Its version `fields` hold the required structure from [KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md](KNOWLEDGE-BASE.md):

```json
{
  "question": "string",
  "answer": "string (partner-facing, precise)",
  "client_explanation": "string (safe to say to a client)",
  "sources": ["web/src/lib/faq-library.ts#hosting-provided"],
  "limitations": "string",
  "escalation": { "required": "always | when | never", "condition": "string", "route": "technical_scoping | commercial_assistance | escalation | …" },
  "aliases": ["other ways people ask it"],
  "topic": "hosting"
}
```

The service validates the shape on write. A knowledge version without a source, limitation or escalation rule cannot move to `in_review`.

## 4. Search: deterministic first

**Recommendation: PostgreSQL full-text search with curated synonyms and exact alias matching. No embeddings, no language model.**

Why:

- Every answer a partner sees must be approved text. Retrieval that returns approved items verbatim is auditable; generated answers are not.
- No AI provider, budget or data-processing agreement is approved ([FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md](../intelligence/FOUNDER-DECISIONS.md)).
- The corpus is small (hundreds of items). PostgreSQL search is fast at that size, already in the stack, and adds no dependency.
- Results are reproducible, so they can be tested.

Design:

1. On publish, the service writes a search document for the version: `setweight(to_tsvector('english', title || question), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', aliases), 'A') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', answer || body), 'B') || setweight(to_tsvector('english', topic), 'C')`. A generated column or a row written in the same transaction keeps it consistent.
2. A founder-managed synonym list (`empower_search_synonyms`: term → canonical term, for example "ssl" → "https certificate", "aeo" → "ai search", "wp" → "wordpress") expands the query before `websearch_to_tsquery`. This is deterministic and reviewable.
3. Ranking: exact alias match first, then `ts_rank_cd` with weights, then topic order. Ties broken by slug, so ordering is stable.
4. Filtering in SQL, never in the browser: `status='published' AND review_by >= current_date AND audience` permitted for the caller.
5. Zero-result queries are logged (query text only, partner id hashed) so founders can see gaps and add aliases. Retention for this log is a founder decision (`AP-PRIV-02`).
6. Optional later step: `pg_trgm` for typo tolerance. It is still deterministic.

What would justify revisiting: a corpus of thousands of items, evidence from zero-result logs that synonyms cannot keep up, and an approved AI provider and data-processing agreement. Even then, the answer shown should be an approved entry, with retrieval-only assistance.

## 5. Rendering

- Bodies are a **restricted Markdown subset**: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, tables, block quotes and links to internal routes or approved external domains. Raw HTML is disabled. Rendering happens on the server, with a sanitising pass as defence in depth.
- Client-facing items render with a visible "Client-facing: approved for sharing" ribbon. Partner-only items render with "Partner only: do not share".
- Every rendered item shows version, approval date and review-by date.
- Copy-to-clipboard is offered only for client-facing items and templates.

## 6. Integration with B0

| B0 system | Integration |
|---|---|
| `expansion_resources` | Keep as is. Migrate existing published rows into `empower_content_items` as `kind='resource'` in Phase 1, or leave them read-only and stop creating new ones. Decision `AP-ENG-01` |
| Onboarding toolkit | Link published handbook, brochure, pricing and commission references to `brochures`, `pricing_documents`, `commission_documents` and `academy` items. Requires the toolkit join to accept Empower items (small change) or the content to remain mirrored in `expansion_resources` |
| Meetings | Every escalation rule names a meeting type. "Request help" in the knowledge viewer opens the existing meeting request form pre-filled with the type and a reference to the entry |
| Audit | Every content write calls the existing `audit()` helper with an `empower_*` event name |
| RBAC | No new role. Reads: `expansion.partner`. Writes and approvals: `expansion.founder`. Founder preview uses the partner renderer with a "preview" banner |
| `partner-programme.ts` | Commercial lessons and the commission reference embed figures by **reference** to the programme constants, rendered with the plan version they come from, so they cannot drift from the engine |

## 7. Feature flags

Following the B0 pattern (everything defaults off):

| Flag | Default | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Resource Centre and knowledge search |
| `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` | `false` | Partner-side Academy |
| `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` | `false` in production until Phase 1 is accepted | Founder content workspace |

With a flag off, partner routes return 404 and the tab is hidden. The founder workspace can be enabled first so content can be loaded and approved before partners see anything.

## 8. Open engineering decisions

| ID | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `AP-ENG-01` | Migrate or freeze `expansion_resources` | Freeze: keep it for toolkit links, create new content in Empower tables, add a read adapter |
| `AP-ENG-02` | Markdown renderer | A small, maintained renderer with HTML disabled; justify the dependency in the PR |
| `AP-ENG-03` | Separate routes or tabs | Separate route segments under `/partner/academy`, `/partner/resources` and `/partner/knowledge`, sharing the portal shell |
| `AP-ENG-04` | Content seeding | A reviewed seed script that loads drafts from this folder as `draft` versions only, never as published |
# Empower security model (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Extends [../SECURITY-MODEL.md](../SECURITY-MODEL.md) and the B0 hardening work. Nothing here changes authentication.

## 1. Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Partner-only content (commission references, objection playbooks, escalation routes) | Internal | Leakage could be read as a commercial offer or misused by competitors |
| Client-facing content | Low once approved; high while draft | A leaked draft could be presented to a client as approved |
| Approval records | Integrity-critical | They are the evidence that content was approved |
| Partner progress | Personal data | Could be used to monitor or direct partners, which bears on independent status |
| Search logs | Personal data (low) | Reveal what an individual partner is working on |

## 2. Roles and capabilities

No new role or capability is required.

| Actor | Capability | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent partner | `expansion.partner` | Read published, in-review-window content for their audience; search; record own progress; request a meeting from an entry | See drafts, approvals, other partners' progress, founder notes or search logs; write content |
| Founder | `expansion.manage` + `expansion.founder` | Draft, review, approve, publish, supersede, archive; see aggregate progress; preview as partner | Approve their own draft when two founders are active (decision `AP-GOV-04`); delete versions |
| Owner, administrator | per `admin/src/lib/rbac.ts` | Whatever their existing capabilities allow | They never hold `expansion.partner`, so they cannot act as a partner |
| Anonymous | none | Nothing | Reach any Empower route (the admin origin requires sign-in) |

## 3. Controls

### 3.1 Audience separation

- Audience is set on the **item**, cannot change, and is checked in SQL on every read.
- Partner-only items carry a "Partner only: do not share" ribbon and no copy button. Client-facing items carry an approval ribbon with the version and date.
- A lint rule in the content service refuses to move a `client_facing` version to `in_review` if its body contains blocked terms (commission, basis points, payout, withdrawal, referral reward, founder-only, internal) unless a founder explicitly overrides with a reason. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.

### 3.2 Publication integrity

- Immutable versions, enforced by a trigger (same approach as `expansion_resource_lifecycle`).
- Approval is a separate, append-only row recorded by a founder, with a reference and a review-by date.
- Publication fails closed: an expired review date, a missing approval or a disabled flag means the item is not served.
- Every transition writes an audit row with the actor and the version id.

### 3.3 Rendering safety

- Restricted Markdown, raw HTML disabled, server-side rendering, then sanitising.
- Links are limited to internal routes and an allow-list of external domains (for example `ico.org.uk`, `gov.uk`). Founders manage the allow-list.
- No file uploads in this scope, so there is no malware-scanning or storage requirement. Photographs remain unsupported, as in B0.

### 3.4 Input handling

- Every write goes through the existing command endpoint pattern with length limits (B0 uses 200 for titles and 30,000 for content).
- `fields` JSON is validated against a schema per `kind` on the server.
- Search input is length-limited (200 characters), passed as a bound parameter to `websearch_to_tsquery`, and rate-limited per partner (the public site's `web/src/lib/rate-limit-policy.ts` is the model; an admin-side equivalent was not verified).

### 3.5 Independence and privacy

- Progress is private to the partner by default. Founders see aggregates only, unless the partner chooses to share (decision `AP-GOV-03`).
- No progress, completion or knowledge-check data is joined to commission, allocation, recognition or achievements. A test should assert that no such query exists.
- Knowledge-check answers are not stored.
- Search logs: query text and a hashed partner id, retained for a founder-approved period (decision `AP-PRIV-02`). The privacy notice must mention them (decision `AP-PRIV-01`).

## 4. Threats and mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|
| A partner presents a draft as approved | Partners never receive drafts; every rendered item shows approval metadata | A partner could paraphrase from memory; covered by the Professional Conduct course and the partner agreement |
| Partner-only commission information reaches a client | Audience on item, lint check, ribbons, no copy button | A partner can still screenshot; agreement and training cover this |
| A stale price or policy is quoted | Review-by dates fail closed; commercial figures embedded by reference to programme constants | A partner may have saved an old copy; versions show "updated since" |
| A founder approves their own mistake | Second-founder approval rule; audit trail | Single-founder periods need an explicit override with a reason |
| Stored XSS through content | No raw HTML, server rendering, sanitiser, link allow-list | Renderer dependency must be kept patched |
| Progress used to direct or monitor partners | Private by default, no joins to commercial tables, voluntary framing | Requires founder discipline and solicitor review (`AP-GOV-02`) |
| Search probing reveals hidden content | Search runs only over published, permitted rows; zero results look the same whether content is hidden or absent | None identified |
| Enumeration of other partners' data | All partner queries keyed by the authenticated actor via `partnerGuard` | None identified |

## 5. Verification expected at implementation

- Service tests for every lifecycle transition, including refusals.
- Real-PostgreSQL tests for the trigger and the one-published-version index, as B0 does for its guards.
- Role tests: a partner cannot reach any founder content action; an owner cannot reach partner routes.
- A browser test that a partner sees no draft, no expired item and no client-facing copy control on partner-only items.
- A test asserting progress tables are not referenced by commercial queries.

13	## C01 Welcome to ScaleSmiths
14	
15	### C01-L1 The ScaleSmiths story in plain words
16	
17	**Sources:** faq:outside-nottingham, faq:established-businesses, faq:wordpress, `web/src/lib/data.ts`.
18	
19	ScaleSmiths is a web and software studio based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire. It works with businesses across the UK and, remotely, with some businesses overseas. Its published work is custom-built: websites and platforms using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes.
20	
21	Most of its client work is with established businesses: organisations that already have customers, a reputation and some evidence (search rankings, enquiries, existing systems) worth protecting. The work usually starts by understanding what already performs before changing anything.
22	
23	What makes ScaleSmiths different is less about technology and more about honesty and accountability. It writes scope down, it does not promise rankings or results it cannot control, and it says plainly when a cheaper or simpler option would serve the client better.
24	
25	**Say it like this:** "ScaleSmiths is a Nottinghamshire web and software studio. They build custom websites and systems for established businesses, and they are very clear about what is included and what is not."
26	
27	**Avoid:** "the best agency", "guaranteed results", "we" (you are not ScaleSmiths staff; see C12), any claim of offices or regional expertise outside what is published.
28	
29	### C01-L2 What we sell
30	
31	**Sources:** `web/src/lib/published-starting-prices.ts`, `web/src/lib/engagement-models.ts`.
32	
33	ScaleSmiths publishes four starting points:
34	
35	| Offer | Published price |
36	|---|---|
37	| Website design and development | From £2,000 |
38	| Growth Partnership | From £350 per month |
39	| Business Growth Audit | £395 |
40	| Managed Business Email | From £15 per month (three 5GB mailboxes, setup included) |
41	
42	It also takes on established-business transformation and custom platforms. These are **never** sold against a website starting price and are scoped after discovery.
43	
44	A starting price is exactly that. The published boundary reads: "A starting price is the entry point for an agreed scope. It is not unlimited development, marketing, support, integrations or a guaranteed result." Prices are in GBP only. ScaleSmiths does not bill in other currencies or publish converted prices.
45	
46	**Rule:** quote only these four figures, always with the boundary. Anything else is a ScaleSmiths proposal.
47

138	## C03 SEO and Digital Growth
139	
140	### C03-L1 What SEO is
141	
142	**Source:** faq:what-is-seo. SEO makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results. It has three parts: technical foundations that let search engines crawl and index pages, content that answers what people actually search for, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work, not a setting.
143	
144	### C03-L2 Local SEO
145	
146	**Source:** faq:what-is-local-seo. Local SEO targets people looking for a provider in a place. It depends on clear service and area descriptions, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.
147	
148	### C03-L3 Technical SEO
149	
150	**Source:** faq:technical-seo. Crawlability and robots rules, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. It rarely wins attention on its own, but content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.
151	
152	### C03-L4 Timescales and guarantees
153	
154	**Sources:** faq:seo-timeline, faq:ranking-guarantees.
155	
156	Technical fixes can change indexation quickly. Content and authority work is measured over months. **No one can guarantee first place on Google**, because rankings depend on Google's systems, competitors and the searcher.
157	
158	**Say it like this:** "No honest agency can promise a position. What ScaleSmiths commits to is the work: technical health, content that matches real searches, credible proof, and measuring progress against a recorded baseline."
159	
160	### C03-L5 Build versus ongoing
161	
162	Search foundations are part of every build. Ongoing SEO (content, authority, measurement and iteration) is separate, scoped as a project or through a Growth Partnership.
163	
164	### C03-L6 SEO and paid search
165	
166	**Source:** faq:seo-and-google-ads. Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly. The right mix depends on urgency, margin and competition. ScaleSmiths will say when paid search is the more honest answer.
167	
168	### C03-L7 What AI search and AEO mean
169	
170	**Sources:** service listing "SEO/AEO landing pages" (`web/src/lib/service-pages.ts`), `web/src/lib/agent-discovery.ts`. *[FOUNDER DECISION `AP-CNT-06`: no published FAQ answer covers AI search yet. This lesson is new wording.]*
171	
172	People increasingly ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) means making a site's content easy for those systems to understand and cite: pages that answer a buyer's real question directly, consistent facts, structured data and FAQ content, and clear service and location pages. ScaleSmiths builds pages this way and describes its own capabilities accurately in machine-readable form.
173	
174	What you must not say: that ScaleSmiths can get a business "into ChatGPT", guarantee being cited, or control what any AI system says. Those systems are run by third parties and change often.
175	
176	**Say it like this:** "Clear, well-structured answers help both search engines and AI assistants understand a business. Nobody can guarantee what an AI tool will say, but we can make sure your site gives it accurate, useful answers to work from."
177	
178	### C03-L8 Diagnosing "not on Google"
179	
180	**Source:** faq:not-on-google. The usual causes, in order: pages not indexed (robots rules, a noindex tag or a staging setting left on); indexed but not matching what people search for; or competing for terms far above the site's authority. Search Console usually separates these quickly, which is why the Business Growth Audit starts there.

218	## C05 Website Migration
219	
220	### C05-L1 Types of migration
221	
222	A platform rebuild (for example WordPress or Shopify to custom), a hosting move, a domain change, or a content-management change. Each has different risks. Many projects combine several.
223	
224	### C05-L2 WordPress and Shopify moves
225	
226	**Sources:** faq:website-migration, faq:rebuilds. ScaleSmiths reviews current code, licences, data, deployment and connected services first, then recommends a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration, whichever the evidence supports. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved onto self-hosted infrastructure.
227	
228	### C05-L3 Redirects and search risk
229	
230	**Source:** faq:seo-rebuild (*owner review flagged*). Any rebuild carries some search risk and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings. Risk is reduced by mapping old URLs to new ones with redirects, carrying over content that performs, preserving metadata and structured data, and checking indexing after launch.

232	### C05-L4 What to collect
233	
234	Who controls the domain and registrar; current hosting; access to the site's admin; Google Search Console and analytics access (if any); a list of integrations (forms, booking, payments, email marketing); any plugin or theme licences; and the business's deadline (for example a hosting contract ending).

237	
238	Nobody knows who controls the domain; the domain is close to expiry; the previous supplier holds all access; unlicensed or abandoned plugins; data held only in the old platform; a hard deadline within weeks. None of these is a reason to walk away, but every one is a reason to escalate early.

242	Every migration goes to **technical scoping** before any price or timeline is discussed. Share what you collected in C05-L4.

There is no salary, guaranteed income, compulsory working hours or sales target. You choose whether to use the Academy. Any future employed role would be a separate offer with its own agreement, and nothing about that is guaranteed.

Never ask a client for passwords; ScaleSmiths uses delegated or scoped access and never asks for registrar passwords through a public form (faq:dns).

6	
7	**Purpose:** give partners a precise, approved answer to the questions prospects actually ask, with a line they may say to the client, the limit of that answer, and when to hand over.

9	**Required fields for every entry** (the service refuses review without them):
10	
11	| Field | Meaning |
12	|---|---|
13	| Question | As a client would ask it, plus aliases |
14	| Answer | Precise partner-facing answer |
15	| Client-friendly explanation | Wording a partner may say or send. Contains no partner-only information |
16	| Source | Repository file and key, or an approved founder document. No source, no entry |
17	| Limitation | What the answer does not cover or must not be stretched to mean |
18	| Escalation | `always`, `when <condition>`, or `never`, with the meeting type |
19	| Approval status | One of the package statuses; later, the recorded approval with reviewer and review-by date |
20

22	
23	**Search approach:** deterministic PostgreSQL full-text search over question, aliases, answer and topic, with a founder-managed synonym list, exact alias matching first and stable ordering. No language model, no embeddings. Only published, in-review-window entries for the caller's audience are searchable. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 4.
24	
25	**Review cadence (proposed, `AP-GOV-06`):** commercial entries every 3 months; service entries every 6 months; any entry immediately when its source file changes. A CI check that flags entries whose source key changed is a Phase 3 candidate.

27	**Topic taxonomy:** hosting, domains, DNS, business email, website security, analytics, SEO, AI search, WordPress migration, redirects, accessibility, e-commerce, booking systems, CRM, custom software, automation, commercial terms, payment schedules, commission, client onboarding.

## Your new website, explained

### What a project includes

Agreed messaging, page structure, a responsive build that works well on phones, search foundations (metadata, canonical URLs, structured data, headings, internal links, indexation controls and page speed) and a clear route from visitor to enquiry, with launch support for that scope. Your proposal is the definitive list.

### What is separate unless your proposal includes it

Hosting, ongoing SEO, content programmes, integrations and open-ended support. Managed business email is also separate unless combined in writing.

### Price

Website design and development starts from £2,000. That is a starting point for an agreed scope, not unlimited design, content, integrations, marketing or support. Your quote is based on your requirements, the complexity of the journeys and systems, and the deliverables we write down.

### Timing

We confirm timing after discovery. Content readiness, integrations, review cycles and technical risk affect the schedule more than the number of pages. The proposal records the delivery range and its assumptions.

### What we need from you

Information about what you sell and who buys it; what your current site does well; any evidence you have (analytics, Search Console, enquiry records); content, images and brand assets; and access to your domain, hosting and any connected systems. Projects move fastest when these are identified early.

### Ownership

Ownership of the bespoke work is set out in the signed project documents and transfers once the agreed fees are paid. You keep your own materials, trademarks and business data.

### Editing your site

If you expect to change content often, we can build an editable content layer. Tell us what you expect to change and how often, and the proposal will say exactly what is editable.

### Moving from your current site

We review what the current site already does well (pages that rank, enquiries, integrations and hosting) before recommending a rebuild, a focused repair or a migration. When we migrate, we map existing URLs to their new equivalents with redirects, carry over content that performs, preserve metadata and check indexing after launch. Any rebuild carries some search risk, and nobody can honestly guarantee rankings.

### Hosting

Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service. We choose it around the workload and support model, and document who is accountable.

## Custom software and automation

### When custom software makes sense

When your workflow genuinely sets you apart, when existing tools create real friction, or when your integration and data-ownership needs cannot be met by configuring a product. If a proven product already meets the need, buying and integrating it is usually the better decision, and we will tell you so.

### What we build

Customer relationship and job management systems, quote and booking workflows, customer and member portals, internal admin systems, payment and subscription integrations, and integrations with the tools you already use. Roles, permissions and sensitive operations are enforced on the server.

*[Placeholder: approved published examples.]*

### Automation

We start with one bounded workflow whose owner, inputs, exceptions and outcome can be defined. Good automation removes repeated handling while keeping the decisions people still need to make. High-consequence steps keep a human review point and a record. Simple rules and integrations are often safer and cheaper than AI; we use AI where interpretation is genuinely required.

### Replacing spreadsheets

Usually gradually: begin with the highest-friction workflow and leave stable processes in place until replacing them is justified.

### How it is priced and delivered

Custom work is scoped after discovery. It is not sold against a website starting price. We define a first release with a clear boundary, design data and permissions for the next stage, and document deployment and operations as part of delivery.

### Payments

Card details stay with the payment provider. Order and subscription status relies on verified server-side events from the provider rather than a browser redirect alone.

## Being found: search and AI search

### What SEO is

Search engine optimisation is the work that makes a website findable, understandable and worth choosing in search results: technical foundations, content that answers real searches, and an on-page experience that turns a click into an enquiry. It is ongoing work.

### Local SEO

For people searching for a provider in a place: clear service and area pages, consistent business details across the web, a Google Business Profile that supports the site, and visible local proof.

### Technical SEO

Crawlability, canonical URLs, sitemaps, redirects, structured data, heading hierarchy, mobile rendering, Core Web Vitals and HTTPS. Content cannot perform if the technical layer works against it.

### AI search and answer engine optimisation (AEO)

*[DRAFT: new wording, founder approval required]* More people now ask AI assistants and AI-generated search summaries for recommendations. Those systems work best with clear, accurate, well-structured information. We build pages that answer buyers' real questions directly, keep facts consistent, and use structured data and FAQ content. Nobody can control or guarantee what an AI system says about a business, because those systems are run by third parties and change often.

### What to expect

Technical fixes can change indexation quickly; content and authority work is measured over months. No one can guarantee first place on Google. We commit to the work, and to measuring it against a recorded baseline.

### In a new build, and afterwards

Search foundations are part of every ScaleSmiths build. Ongoing SEO is separate: a project, or part of a Growth Partnership.

### Paid search

Ads buy visibility immediately and stop when the budget does; SEO compounds slowly. We will tell you when paid search is the more honest answer for your timeframe.

### Not sure where you stand?

The Business Growth Audit (£395) reviews indexation, technical health, content coverage, internal linking and the conversion journey, and produces a prioritised roadmap. Where the published terms apply, the full fee is credited against an eligible subsequent ScaleSmiths build.

# Empower acceptance criteria (proposed)

**Status: DRAFT.** Each criterion should be verified by an automated test unless marked *(manual)*. Phases are defined in [IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md](IMPLEMENTATION-PHASES.md).

## Phase 0: planning package

- [x] Package exists under `docs/expansion/empower/` with architecture, curriculum, lesson content, resource drafts, knowledge inventory, wireframes, approval register, phases, acceptance criteria and security model.
- [x] Every item carries an approval status; no item is marked approved.
- [x] `node scripts/check-documentation-links.mjs` passes.
- [ ] Founders have reviewed the package *(manual)*.

## Phase 1: content foundation

**Lifecycle and integrity**
1. A version's title, body, fields, sources, author and creation time cannot be updated; attempts fail at the database.
2. Versions cannot be deleted.
3. Only the transitions in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) section 3.1 succeed; all others fail at both service and database.
4. `in_review → approved` fails without an approval row by a founder; fails when the approver is the author while two founders are active; succeeds with a recorded override reason when only one founder is active.
5. Publishing a version supersedes the previous published version in the same transaction; at most one published version per item exists, including under concurrent publishes (real-PostgreSQL test on separate connections).
6. An item's audience cannot be changed after creation.
7. Every transition writes an audit row with actor, item, version and event.

**Validation**
8. A knowledge version without question, answer, client explanation, source, limitation or escalation cannot be submitted.
9. A client-facing version containing blocked terms cannot be submitted without an override reason, which is audited.
10. Links outside internal routes and the allow-list are rejected.
11. Rendered output contains no raw HTML from the body; script and event-handler payloads are neutralised (renderer tests with known XSS vectors).

**Access**
12. A partner account receives 403 for every founder content action and the founder Content workspace.
13. An owner or administrator cannot reach any `/partner` route (existing RBAC rule still holds).
14. With `EMPOWER_FOUNDER_CONTENT_ENABLED` off, the Content workspace is not reachable.

**Seeding**
15. The seed script creates only `draft` versions and is idempotent.

## Phase 2: Resource Centre and knowledge search

**Serving**
1. Partners receive only versions that are `published`, within `review_by`, and permitted for their audience; drafts, approved-but-unpublished, superseded, archived and expired versions are never returned (service and browser tests).
2. Audience filtering happens in SQL; no request parameter can widen it.
3. Every rendered item shows audience ribbon, version, approval date and review-by date.
4. Copy controls appear only on client-facing content.
5. With `PARTNER_RESOURCE_CENTRE_ENABLED` off, partner routes return 404 and navigation hides them.

**Search**
6. Identical queries over identical content return identical ordering.
7. Exact alias matches rank above full-text matches.
8. Synonyms expand queries as configured (for example "ssl" finds the HTTPS entry).
9. A search never returns unpublished, expired or other-audience content, and a zero-result response is identical whether matching content is hidden or absent.
10. Query input over 200 characters is rejected; search is rate-limited per partner.
11. Zero-result queries are logged with a hashed partner id and purged after the approved retention period.
12. p95 search latency under 200ms with 1,000 published entries on CI hardware.

**Integration**
13. "Request help" opens a meeting request pre-filled with the entry's escalation type and reference; nothing is booked automatically.
14. Legacy published `expansion_resources` appear in the library through the read adapter, labelled as legacy.

**Experience** *(manual plus automated accessibility checks)*
15. Knowledge search, resource library and objection workspace are usable at 320px width without horizontal scrolling.
16. Automated accessibility checks report no serious or critical violations; colour-contrast tokens meet the values in [DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md](DESIGN-SPECIFICATION.md).
17. All functions are keyboard operable; `/` focuses search.

## Phase 3: Partner Academy

1. Courses, modules and lessons appear only when their content versions are published and within review.
2. Progress is visible only to the partner who created it; founders see aggregate counts only, unless the partner has opted in (if `AP-GOV-03` allows it).
3. No query from commission, allocation, recognition, achievements, referrals or withdrawals reads progress tables (static test over the server modules).
4. Knowledge-check answers are not persisted; only `check_attempted` is stored.
5. No course is marked required, and no UI text uses "must complete", "deadline" or "score" (copy test).
6. When a lesson is superseded, partners who read the old version see "Updated since you read it".
7. With `PARTNER_ACADEMY_ENABLED` off, Academy routes return 404.
8. Lesson pages meet the same width, keyboard and contrast criteria as Phase 2.

# Empower design specification

**Status: DRAFT.** Visual direction for the Academy, Resource Centre and founder publishing interface. Screen-level layouts are in [WIREFRAMES.md](WIREFRAMES.md). Brand changes need founder approval (`AP-DES-01`).

## 1. Direction

**Quiet premium.** Black and charcoal surfaces, metallic gold used sparingly as a signal of quality and of "approved", silver for secondary emphasis, generous spacing, clear typography, minimal navigation. The interface should feel calm and trustworthy: a partner is about to speak to a client and needs the right answer fast. Search comes first; decoration never competes with content.

Principles:

1. **Content first.** Text measures 60 to 75 characters on large screens; nothing decorative inside reading areas.
2. **Gold means something.** Gold marks primary actions, the active item and approval ribbons. It is not used for body text or large fills.
3. **Status is never colour alone.** Every status has a text label and an icon.
4. **Mobile is a first-class target.** Partners will read lessons and look up answers on phones before meetings.
5. **Reuse before invent.** Build on the admin tokens and the `ex-*` portal patterns.

## 2. Reconciling the two existing systems

The Partner Portal is part of the admin app, so Empower uses the **admin token set** as its base and borrows silver from the public site. It does not import the public site's warm palette wholesale, which would make the portal inconsistent with the rest of the admin shell.

| Role | Empower token | Value | Origin | Contrast (measured) |

| Raised surface | `--s1` | `#1a1b1e` | admin | — |
| Card surface | `--s2` | `#222428` | admin | — |
| Hover surface | `--s3` | `#2a2d31` | admin | — |
| Primary text | `--t1` | `#f1f5f9` | admin | 16.82:1 on `--bg` |
| Secondary text | `--t2` | `#a6b0be` | admin | 7.85:1 on `--s1`; 7.09:1 on `--s2` |
| Muted text (new) | `--emp-muted` | `#8a93a3` | new | 5.95:1 on `--bg`; 5.02:1 on `--s2` |
| Decorative text only | `--t3` | `#667085` | admin | **3.71:1 on `--bg`: fails AA for body text**; use only for disabled states and decoration |

| Gold gradient (decoration) | `--emp-gold` | `linear-gradient(135deg,#e6cf8f 0%,#d1b266 45%,#a8873f 100%)` | new, from `--acc` | Dark text `#131416` on it: 5.44:1 at the darkest stop |

Contrast values were calculated with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula (the same method as `web/src/lib/color-contrast.ts`). They must be asserted in tests at implementation, as the public site already does.

**Clean-up recommended alongside:** `expansion.css` hard-codes `#131416`, `#18191b`, `#edf0f5` and `#c3a86c`. Empower styles should use tokens only; replacing the hard-coded portal values is a small, separate change (`AP-ENG-05`).

## 3. Typography

| Use | Family | Size / line height | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Display (course titles, page titles) | `--font-syne` (admin resolves this to Arial Black) | 28/34 desktop, 24/30 mobile | 700 |
| Section heading | Inter | 20/28 | 600 |
