Decision `AP-DES-02`: whether to self-host Syne in the admin app (as the public site does) so display type matches the brand. Until decided, the existing fallback stays.

## 4. Layout and spacing

- 8px spacing grid; page gutter 16px mobile, 24px tablet, 36px desktop (matching `.ex-header`).
- Max content width 1200px; reading column 720px.
- Radius: 8px cards (admin `--radius-md`), 12px feature panels (as `.ex-research`), 999px chips.
- Elevation: borders before shadows; `--shadow-raised` only for overlays.
- Breakpoints: 640px, 960px, 1280px.

## 5. Components

| Component | Specification | Reuses |
|---|---|---|
| Portal shell | Existing header and tab navigation. Empower adds three entries: Academy, Resources, Knowledge | `ExpansionWorkspace` items |
| Search bar | Full width, 52px tall, silver 1px border, gold focus ring (3px, `rgba(209,178,102,.28)`), keyboard shortcut `/` | `.field-control` pattern |
| Course card | `--s2` surface, 2px gold-gradient top edge, overline (course number), title, one-line purpose, lesson count and reading time, progress ring (private), status chip | `.ex-panel` |

| Audience ribbon | Full-width strip above content: silver "Partner only: do not share" or gold-outlined "Client-facing: approved for sharing" | new |

| Knowledge result | Question (heading), client explanation (first), limitation, escalation, source, status chip | new |
| Copy control | Only on client-facing text; announces "Copied" via `aria-live` | new |
| Empty state | One sentence and a next action, as in the existing `Empty` component | `Empty` |
| Founder diff view | Side-by-side or inline diff between versions, additions in green, removals struck through, with labels | new |

## 6. Motion

Subtle and optional: 150 to 200ms fades for panels and chips, no parallax, no animated gradients. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (the admin already does for its workspace).

## 7. Accessibility requirements

- WCAG 2.2 AA as the target for these screens (an engineering target, not a public claim).
- Full keyboard operation, visible focus, logical heading order, skip link to search.
- Status conveyed by text and icon as well as colour.
- Lesson text resizable to 200% without horizontal scrolling at 320px width.
- Knowledge checks: answers announced via `aria-live`; no time limits.

[outside-nottingham] Yes. ScaleSmiths is based in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire and works with businesses across the UK. Published work also includes CSDS, a computer repair firm in Pennsylvania. Projects outside the area, including work with businesses overseas, run remotely with a review cadence agreed in the scope. We do not claim overseas offices or regional expertise we cannot substantiate. Proposals are quoted in GBP.

[established-businesses] Yes, and that is where most of the client work sits. Confirm-A-Kill is an established Nottinghamshire pest-control business whose website and operating systems were rebuilt around search, conversion and day-to-day delivery. Established businesses usually have real evidence === rankings, enquiries, existing systems === and the work starts by protecting what already performs.

[hosting-provided] Yes. Published work runs on self-hosted Docker Compose and Nginx setups on a VPS as well as managed platforms such as Vercel, chosen around the workload and the support model rather than sold as an anonymous storage allowance. Hosting can be arranged as part of a build or as a managed service on its own.

[business-email] Yes. ScaleSmiths Managed Business Email starts at £15 per month for three custom-domain mailboxes with 5GB of storage each, and initial mailbox and DNS setup is included at no additional setup charge. It covers webmail, desktop and mobile client compatibility, aliases and forwarding, spam filtering, TLS-secured transport, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration. It is available standalone, you do not need a ScaleSmiths website.

[deposit] Payment terms, including any staged or upfront payment, are set out in the proposal and signed order for each project rather than published as a blanket policy. Ownership of bespoke deliverables transfers once the applicable agreed fees are paid. Ask during discovery and you will have the terms in writing before anything is committed.

[ecommerce-builds] Yes. Pinkys Prints is a custom e-commerce platform with catalogue variants and a tailored product admin, migrated from Shopify. We recommend custom commerce only when the operational value justifies owning it; where an established platform already fits, configuring and integrating it is usually the better decision.

[integrations] Usually, yes. Published work includes a Salon Tracker booking integration and Google and Facebook review aggregation for Glow Tanning, and Stripe subscription billing with LiveKit video for The Business Circle. We check the existing system's API, data and ownership before committing to an approach, because not every tool exposes what an integration needs.

[crm] Yes, where an off-the-shelf CRM does not fit the workflow. Confirm-A-Kill runs on a private PostgreSQL-backed CRM covering enquiries, customers, properties, quotations, appointments, jobs, visits and commercial service records; CSDS has a quote management admin panel behind its website. If an existing CRM already does the job, connecting the website to it is often the better investment.

[stripe] Yes. The Business Circle runs Stripe subscription billing for tiered memberships, and Prymal uses Stripe for plans, team seats and execution credits. Card details stay with the payment provider === we do not create a reason to handle them directly === and order or subscription state relies on verified server-side provider events rather than a browser redirect alone.

[customer-portals] Yes. ScaleSmiths runs its own client portal for projects, invoices, documents, messages and requests, with tenant isolation enforced server-side. The Business Circle is a published membership platform with tiered access, and VeteranFinder includes member and admin applications. Permissions and tenant boundaries are enforced on the server rather than treated as interface options.

[internal-admin-systems] Yes. Admin surfaces are a recurring part of published work: quote management for CSDS, product and catalogue administration for Pinkys Prints, content administration for Glow Tanning, member management for The Business Circle, and a dedicated admin console for VeteranFinder. Roles, permissions and sensitive operations are enforced server-side.

[website-ownership] Ownership of the bespoke deliverable, along with content, accounts and any third-party services, is set out in the signed project documents, and transfer follows once the agreed fees are paid. ScaleSmiths keeps its own pre-existing tools, frameworks and know-how, and open-source components stay under their own licences. The client service terms state this in full.

[backups] Backups are part of a managed hosting or maintenance arrangement, and the order states which environments, data and retention are covered. We are deliberately plain about the limits: backups reduce risk but do not make loss impossible, they do not replace your own continuity responsibilities, and no restoration guarantee, recovery point or recovery time is created by our online terms. Ask, and the actual arrangement is written into the agreement.

[ssl] Yes. HTTPS is a build standard, not an upsell, and certificate provisioning and renewal are part of managed hosting and deployment. The specific arrangement depends on where the site runs: platform-managed certificates on a host such as Vercel, or certificates managed at the Nginx layer on a VPS deployment.

[dns] Yes, where you give us appropriate access. Managed Business Email onboarding includes configuring the required mail and authentication records, and website or hosting work includes the DNS changes a launch or migration needs. We use delegated or scoped access where it is supported, and we never ask for domain or registrar passwords through a public form.

[after-enquiry] The founders review what you send and reply with a sensible next step. That may be a few clarifying questions, a recommendation to start with the Business Growth Audit, or a proposal once the scope is understood. What can be committed to is the work itself: technical health, content that matches real search intent, credible proof, and measurement against a recorded baseline so progress is judged on evidence.

[wordpress] The websites and platforms in our published work are custom builds using technologies such as Next.js, React, Astro, Node.js and PostgreSQL rather than WordPress themes. If you already run WordPress, we look at what it is doing well before recommending whether a rebuild is justified.

[website-migration] Often, after a technical review of the current code, licence terms, data, deployment process and connected services. Pinkys Prints is a published example: a Shopify store rebuilt as a custom platform and moved from managed cloud services onto self-hosted infrastructure. We map existing URLs, metadata and internal links before a migration to reduce avoidable search disruption.

[hosting-included] Not automatically. Hosting can be part of a Growth Partnership or arranged as a managed hosting service on its own, and the order states which applications, environments, monitoring, maintenance and backups are covered. Managed Business Email is likewise separate unless a combined arrangement is written into the agreement.

## 1. Method and sources of authority

B0 still can't be merged properly, so I haven't started building B1. I did finish the full audit of all 27 B1 planning documents. The corrections are pushed to the planning branch as commit `605a03a`, and the description of [PR #156](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/156) is updated. Nothing is approved: this was a model review, not a human one.

## Why B0 is blocked (re-checked today)

[PR #155](https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/pull/155) is ready on the engineering side: still a draft, mergeable, at head `4e713e5`, with all 21 CI, Security and CodeQL checks passing. The problem is governance:
- **No eligible reviewer.** Every path in CODEOWNERS belongs to `@TheFridey`, who is also the PR author and the only collaborator. GitHub doesn't let an author approve their own PR, so the required review can't happen.
- **No protection on `master`.** It returns "Branch not protected" and has no rulesets, so GitHub would accept a merge today. That's a reason not to merge, not permission to.
- I approved nothing, changed no settings and merged nothing. PR #156 stays based on the B0 branch, because retargeting it to `master` now would pull all of B0 into its diff.

## What the audit found

All 27 files were read in full and checked against the code and published sources. All 61 FAQ answers the docs cite exist, all 29 file paths exist, and every contrast ratio recalculates correctly. Fixed in this commit:
- **Lesson count:** there are 91 lessons in 38 modules, not 94 as the PR description said. There are no gaps or duplicates, and every lesson has text.
- **Commercial:**
  - Earlier six-month agreements (£4,100 minimum) were never mentioned. They're now described as historical terms that existing clients keep.
  - The "splitting payments can't change commission" claim now applies only to the current plans.
  - Refunds are described as recorded reversals, not automatic deductions.
  - "No market is approved, including the UK" is now worded as the software's starting state rather than a permanent fact.
  - Worked examples are labelled as illustrations, not earnings forecasts. Commission is stated plainly as one-off, with no monthly commission.
- **Accessibility:** the proposed muted text colour `#8a93a3` failed the contrast standard on hover backgrounds (4.47:1), so it's now `#939cac`. The existing admin muted colour `#667085` fails on every background: it's used 68 times in 36 files plus 72 times as a class in 15 more. I recorded that for a separate, reviewed change rather than altering it globally.
- **Security:** blocking revoked or suspended partners is now specified, with tests to prove it. The existing partner check already does this.
- **Other:**
  - The objection playbook now gives each response's limits and the resource that backs it.
  - The opt-out follow-up template is flagged for legal and privacy review.
  - The approval register has 11 new, unapproved decision rows.

## Not done or not checked

- **Knowledge-check questions don't exist yet**, apart from one example question in course 1. The course outlines give only a question count, so there were no quiz answers to check. I've recorded this as deferred.
- I didn't fetch external sources such as the ICO guidance, or look at production settings.
- Accessibility was checked from the colour tokens only. There are no B1 screens to test yet.

The register is in [CONTENT-REVIEW-REGISTER.md](docs/expansion/empower/CONTENT-REVIEW-REGISTER.md) and the gate status in [B1-STATUS.md](docs/expansion/empower/B1-STATUS.md). The three uncommitted files in the main checkout were left untouched.

The way forward is your call as repository owner. Either add a second reviewer and apply the protection policy, or record a documented solo-maintainer exception. Once B0 is properly merged, I'll retarget PR #156 and start B1 on `feature/operation-empower`.
